market.headline: Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO set off a sharp tech bounce after the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020. SPY and QQQ still closed below their 20-, 50- and 200-day averages, and the regime is still red.
market.day_type: Relief bounce led by one stock's news. Nvidia's board reversed course and brought back its CEO, and that pulled the whole AI chain up on 1.5x normal volume, with the most-sold names (NVDA, CRWV, MU, ARM) bouncing hardest.
watch: Tonight and Tuesday: HPE and CRWD results, then Dell and ADI, are a direct test of AI server and chip demand (SMCI, NVDA, AVGO).
Wed Nov 25, 08:30: GDP and PCE inflation. After the close, Fed's Williams said rates likely go higher over time, and the 10-year is at 5.04.
QQQ 641.95 (today's low): a break below it means the bounce has failed. A close above 675.47 (20-day average) is the first sign of a real turn.

stocks.headline: Up 31.5% to 165.05 on 2.7x normal volume after the board voted Huang back as CEO. Morning call: right, because the 143.73 trigger fired at the open.
stocks.why: The slide was about leadership and China, not the business. Last quarter EPS was 2.68 vs 2.47 expected, sales grew 106%, next year's forecasts are up 28% in 90 days, and the stock trades at 8x forward profit. Huang's return removes the biggest unknown, and it lifted TSM, MU, ARM, SMCI and CRWV with it. The new risk is political: members of Congress from both parties are attacking the decision on national-security grounds, and the China chip-shipment problem has not gone away.

long_term.reason: The house view is Wait. We move up one step because the reason to wait, no CEO, is gone, and a business growing this fast at its lowest valuation in 5 years is cheap.

stocks.what_would_change_it: Washington moving to restrict Nvidia's leadership or its China sales would send this back to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't chase 165. Buy a first piece only on a pullback that holds 156.93 after the first hour, and sell any new shares if it closes below 143.73.

levels.means: above = today's gap is holding and buyers are in control; below = the gap is being sold
above = the reversal still stands; below = the bounce failed, so step aside
above = a new leg up toward the 20-day average 178.91; below = stuck in today's range

stocks.headline: Up 12.3% to 113.68 with the AI bounce. Morning call: wrong, because the dip to 101.19 never came.
stocks.why: Oracle is a bet on AI data-center contracts. Its 664.0B backlog dwarfs its 71.8B of yearly sales, sales are speeding up (+30%), and it trades at 9x forward profit, its cheapest in 5 years. It rose today because the selloff was about AI spending fear, not Oracle's own numbers. The risk is the Dec 14 report: analysts expect EPS down 16%, the company gave no outlook, and the stock usually moves about 11% on results. Higher rates also weigh on it.

long_term.reason: Agrees with the house view: a contracted backlog at a 5-year-low valuation, and earnings forecasts are steady.

stocks.what_would_change_it: If the Dec 14 report shows customers delaying or shrinking data-center contracts, the backlog case breaks.
stocks.action: Buy the first third tomorrow only if it holds 112.28 after the first hour. If 112.28 breaks, wait and buy at 100.25 instead.

levels.means: above = buyers are defending the bounce, so buy the first third; below = it drifts back toward the lows
above = the short-term downtrend is broken, so add the second third; below = still a bounce
above = the 52-week low holds and is the best place to buy; below = the thesis needs the Dec 14 report to rescue it

stocks.headline: Up 19.0% to 707.7, back above Friday's 669.0 high. Morning call: right.
stocks.why: Memory was hit hardest in the AI selloff, yet the business is at a peak. Sales rose 345% last quarter with a 75% operating margin, the backlog is 134.0B, and cash of 38.4B covers 2.8B of debt many times over. At 3x forward profit the market is betting the cycle turns, and memory cycles turn fast. The stock moves about twice the Nasdaq in both directions and still sits under its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages. It reports Dec 17 with no outlook given.

long_term.reason: Agrees with the house view. The numbers are the strongest in the group, but the chart is still broken, and it needs to prove the low is in before Dec 17.
